title: 8-round AES-192: Impossible differential, low-data endpoint

target.description: Standard AES-192 under the paper's round numbering: initial whitening k0, rounds1 onward; last MixColumns omitted for 8-round recovery variants. Guess13 bytes0,1,2,4,5,7,8,10,11,12,13,14,15 of k8 and byte3 of w7, then recover8 whitening bytes:176 bits of named subkey material. These are selected round-key values, not an independently priced complete192-bit master key.

setting.key_relation: Two unknown AES-192 master keys K and K'=K XOR Delta, where Delta[0]=Delta[8]=a!=0 and the other22 bytes are0. Initial whitening is k0; round subkeys are k1,... .
setting.key_population: General unknown key pair with attacker-chosen nonzero a; b,c are actual key-dependent S-box output differences, not independently chosen subkeys.
setting.plaintext_model: Two pools of2^63.5 plaintexts; total2^64.5 queries. A2^-56 filter leaves about2^71 usable pairs per outer hypothesis.
assumptions: The source models pair filters and incorrect whitening-key eliminations probabilistically; those independence assumptions have not been proved for every AES key.
Named subkey bits may be dependent. No complete192-bit master-key recovery budget is supplied.
The source uses64 memory accesses per encryption equivalent; this is an accounting convention, not an independent implementation measurement.
The112-bit terminal guess computes b and c through the source's schedule relations.

time.note: Source formula uses2^71 retained pairs,2^112 terminal hypotheses, a2^-6 memory-access conversion. Remaining master-key completion is not priced.

data.note: Total plaintext-block encryption queries across exactly2 related keys, not a per-key budget.

memory.note: Author-reported memory; do not reinterpret the exponent as128-bit blocks.

preprocessing.note: The shared Section4 precomputation is about2^62 encryptions; no complete additional setup total for this extension is separately supplied.

success.description: No numerical recovery success is supplied for this 176-bit named-subkey output. The source uses2^71 useful pairs and a small conditional wrong-list estimate; it does not quantify joint output recovery. Keep the existing missing-Delta filtering-notation conflict; the component retention statement is conditional on the intended difference equations, not the disputed literal notation. Remaining master-key completion stays unpriced.

Section5.2 reuses the uniform-elimination procedure with2^71 useful pairs for one fixed wrong64-bit whitening candidate. For the first variant the source2^-8 is an expected aggregate suggestion count over2^112 terminal guesses, not a whole-output failure probability.

PDF10 / printed24 Section5.2 First Attack: author-model upper bound on at least one wrong64-bit whitening candidate for ONE fixed112-bit terminal-key hypothesis after approximately2^71 usable pairs. Source rounds it to2^-120 and then counts approximately2^-8 expected suggestions over all2^112 hypotheses. This bound is not the probability of correct176-bit output or complete AES192 recovery; intended difference equations and the existing notation conflict remain.

Preserve source-model components, intended-difference conditions, missing-Delta and per-bin conflicts. Not a new full-paper audit.
